utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: By this stage -- and we can find it in the document, if necessary, but it's here to record matters -- by this stage how was the progress with the removal of checkpoints? How was progress with exchange of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: The exchange of prisoners was, as far as I could check it, and I checked personally with most of the presence in the area, was really fulfilled, no prisoners. Only in one prison I saw some, as they call it, criminals, thieves and so on, and the other prisons were empty. The checkpoints almost changes every day. Sometimes they were removed and after a few days they were again manned. We succeeded in manning the checkpoints by civil police and mixed police from Croatic and Croatian Muslim side. Only -- I mean three checkpoints in the area of Novi Travnik, Zenica, and Vitez have been always there and manned by soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next document is 570.1, being an agreement under the heading of the co-ordination committee of the joint commission. Do you remember this agreement?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: The joint commission was accepted at that time by ECMM, and they accepted also the great importance. So we got -- how do I say that -- more important commanders, leaders, than we as a common ECMM. And that was the result of -- that results in the agreement signed by -- at that time, I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you go over the following page, we can see the limited number of signatures.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Hadzihasanovic, Karic, Stewart.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: And Jean-Pierre Thebault. I mean, that was the head of the ECMM mission at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there much confidence in this plan?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: Yes, as every plan we made, but we were often disappointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And so far as this plan was concerned?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: It was at the end of my mission, so I -- one of my -- now, the most important thing of my mission was at that time to remove all the checkpoints, and that was what I checked every day, and it was one of the results were almost fulfilled. I already mentioned the checkpoints were not removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Part of your duty under -- or part of the duties under this agreement was to investigate complaints of harassment by Muslims. Were there much such complaints?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: Yes. There were complaints. It depends on the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was there any particular complaint concerning a Muslim on a bridge close to the camp, that you recall?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: On the bridge near the Dutch company, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: Yes, I heard they reported me that there was shooting at a Muslim man on the bridge near the Dutch alpha company in Busovaca. The man was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The final document, 573 -- final two documents, 573,1 and 599,1. These documents --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I just want to inform you that document 573,1 has already been numbered. So maybe it can be 573,2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The documents that you have before you -- I'm sorry about that. The documents that you have before you, they tell us something about the state of checkpoints at the time of your departure from the area.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: All the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: About the manning of the checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: The manning of the checkpoints. One of them -- subject from agreement was to man the checkpoints by both parties and not by soldiers. Most of the checkpoints were at the moment from my report manned by civil police. And some of them also mixtured -- I called that mixtured Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So when we look at the document 573 with a point 1 or point 2, if you look at that document that's in front of you at the moment, and we look at -- first of all, tell us what this document is. So far as you understand it, what is this document, Mr. Van der Pluijm?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: It's the document I made for myself to check the checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The first entry is "NO2 Bilesevo," and then there is a reference to civil police from the local police at Kakanj. Interpret that entry very briefly with the conclusion you've already told us about in mind.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: You mean that I have to declare or to say --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Explain the entry, yes.

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: Yes, it's only -- it's on the road from Zenica to Kakanj, half -- no, near Kakanj, and they had just a little house in which they had their headquarters manned by -- I said before, two policemen from both sides, and some as a reserve in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So the presence of policemen -- sorry. So the presence of policemen, as opposed to merely the military, represented some progress for the joint commission?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then the last -- so that's one example. If we go to the very last document, 599,1. Go over in this report -- I'm sorry, my mistake. Yes. It's on the first sheet. utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: We call that black point because they didn't fulfill our agreements according to manning of the checkpoints. A checkpoint manned by soldiers with sometimes heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So progress on checkpoints, but not complete success?

utterances.speaker: CORNELIUS VAN DER PLUIJM
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's all I ask of this witness.
